nodes.rationale: Unticked types (TOIL) are earned, not accrued: no policy of their own; their pot borrows the annual-leave policy's leave year and rounding.

nodes.label: Bank holiday handling (closed / pot / included in annual leave)
nodes.norm_label: bank holiday handling (closed / pot / included in annual leave)

nodes.label: Bank holidays and closed days calendar
nodes.norm_label: bank holidays and closed days calendar

nodes.label: Calendar label
nodes.rationale: Shown to everyone, so kept generic (Leave, Sick, Away).

nodes.label: Carry-over cap (carry_over_max_weeks / carry_over_days)
nodes.rationale: Blank means nothing carries; seeded policies leave it blank.

nodes.label: Earned expires after days
nodes.rationale: How long earned TOIL may be used (365 as seeded); 0 refused as it would expire TOIL the day it was earned.

nodes.label: Entitlement (days_per_year / weeks_per_year)
nodes.rationale: Stored in weeks times the contracted weekly amount; hours types enter full-time days stored as days / 5.

nodes.label: Leave policy
nodes.rationale: Policies are data: leave rules per contract type and pot-backed type are rows, not code; saving one recalculates every open pot it can change.

nodes.label: Uses pot flag
nodes.rationale: Ticked with no policy makes requests fail naming the missing policy rather than silently costing nothing.

nodes.label: Contract type
nodes.rationale: Configurable rows (adding a kind of staff is data, not code); unit and full-time weekly amount are the only inputs to FTE.

nodes.label: Fixed absence type codes (AL, BH, SICK, TOIL, MAT, PAT, SPL, ADOPT)
nodes.norm_label: fixed absence type codes (al, bh, sick, toil, mat, pat, spl, adopt)
nodes.rationale: Services look these up by code, so a code is read-only once set and must not be reused or retired; nothing else in code tests a type's name.

nodes.label: Historic terms (TUPE) as separate contract types
nodes.norm_label: historic terms (tupe) as separate contract types
nodes.rationale: A group on different terms needs no code: create a contract type per group with its own policy.

nodes.label: Leave year basis (fixed date / anniversary of start)
nodes.norm_label: leave year basis (fixed date / anniversary of start)
nodes.rationale: Cannot change once pots exist because pots keep the dates they were opened with and each day counts only toward its own leave year's pot.

nodes.label: Moving a type in use to a January year
nodes.norm_label: moving a type in use to a january year
nodes.rationale: End the April policy and add a January one so each day counts once and the April pots' carry-in lands in the January pot.

nodes.label: Recording leave for someone else
nodes.rationale: Approved at once because the person recording it is the one who would have approved it.

nodes.label: Request costing from the working pattern
nodes.norm_label: request costing from the working pattern

nodes.label: Spanning absences clipped to the month
nodes.norm_label: spanning absences clipped to the month
nodes.rationale: Consecutive months never report the same day twice; each month is rounded on its own, so payroll should work from monthly figures.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/absences
nodes.rationale: No field carries the illness category and the type name is never sent.

nodes.label: HR_API_TOKENS bearer tokens
nodes.rationale: One token per client so each can be retired alone; compared in constant time and never logged; none set means every request is refused.

nodes.label: Rota read API (/api/v1/)
nodes.rationale: Read-only and pull-based: the rota asks, nothing is pushed or written.

nodes.label: Employee
nodes.rationale: The person, created once; nothing dated lives on it because a person can leave and come back and history must survive that.

nodes.label: Employee User field (link to login account)
nodes.norm_label: employee user field (link to login account)
nodes.rationale: This link, not the work email, is what sign-in uses for employee_id; without it hr_nightly has no account to disable.

nodes.label: Work email
nodes.rationale: Unique case-insensitively; sign-in does not read it; keep it the same as the login email because the rota matches its own accounts by the email it receives.

nodes.label: Per-app admin roles (Apps section)
nodes.rationale: Controls only who is an admin of each relying party; anyone with an active login can sign in to every registered app.

nodes.label: Login account
nodes.rationale: Separate from an Employee; created with only an email and admin flag.

nodes.label: Nightly housekeeping (hr_nightly)
nodes.rationale: 01:30 daily and idempotent; disables leavers' logins, never re-enables; also runs the year end, opens pots, charges bank holidays and chases waiting requests.

nodes.label: register_oidc_client command
nodes.rationale: Prints client_secret once (stored hashed); --rotate issues a new secret and kills the old one.

nodes.label: The read API for the rota (admin reference)
nodes.norm_label: the read api for the rota (admin reference)

nodes.label: Login accounts and signing in (admin reference)
nodes.norm_label: login accounts and signing in (admin reference)

nodes.label: Match people by id, not email
nodes.norm_label: match people by id, not email
nodes.rationale: The /people email is the work email, which can differ from the login email the rota receives at sign-in, so joining on email is unsafe; id equals the employee_id claim.

nodes.label: API rate limit (API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE)
nodes.rationale: Counted before the token check so a token-guessing client is slowed too; kept in each worker's memory, so it slows guessing rather than metering a good client.

nodes.label: Deactivating a login
nodes.rationale: Deactivate rather than delete: a login that wrote to the audit log cannot be deleted, and deletion would remove Django's record of its admin changes.

nodes.label: import_logins migration from the rota
nodes.rationale: Moves password hashes so nobody chooses a new password and rota admins stay admins; all-or-nothing; run once because re-running restores rota admin flags over later Apps changes.

nodes.label: Invitations and password links
nodes.rationale: Links last seven days and work once; nobody, not even an HR admin, ever sees anyone's password; without email the admin is shown the link once.

nodes.label: Sign-in lockouts (axes)
nodes.rationale: Five wrong passwords lock an email for an hour; an address locks after five different emails fail; retries do not restart the hour so nobody can keep a colleague out; passkeys and email links still work during a lockout.

nodes.label: OpenID Connect provider
nodes.rationale: Consent is skipped because relying parties are practice-operated apps; since a session here is a session in the rota, sessions end at browser close or after 12 hours and sign-out is shared, protecting shared surgery PCs; PKCE required, RS256 tokens expire in ten minutes, only the authorization-code flow.

nodes.label: OIDC_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE signing key
nodes.rationale: Kept in its own file because systemd's environment-file parser turns an unquoted \n into n and breaks a one-line PEM key; never changed once a relying party is registered because rotating invalidates tokens they trust; unset switches the provider off.

nodes.label: Passkeys
nodes.rationale: Adding one needs a recent password and emails the owner, so someone at an unattended signed-in computer cannot quietly add their own; bound to the site's host.

nodes.label: Request logging (hr.access, journal)
nodes.rationale: One line per request with no query strings and password-link tokens replaced by <redacted>; also logs server errors, CSRF failures, disallowed hosts and axes lockouts.

nodes.label: Retention report
nodes.rationale: Lists people past their retention period per category (personal, pay, health, audit); deletes nothing because deletion is a manual decision in this release.

nodes.label: CI pipeline (tests.yml)
nodes.rationale: Runs ruff (pyflakes only), makemigrations --check, the pytest suite, and collectstatic + check --deploy against a throwaway environment; the required ruleset needs it green.

nodes.label: HTTPS redirect (SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT)
nodes.rationale: Trusts cloudflared's X-Forwarded-Proto, one more reason gunicorn binds to loopback only.

nodes.label: MEDIA_ROOT (payroll report storage)
nodes.rationale: Production points it at /var/lib/practice-hr/media because the code tree is read-only; Django never serves it, the payroll page streams reports to HR admins.

nodes.label: Nightly local backup (hr-backup.timer)
nodes.rationale: SQLite copy every night plus a media/ archive, kept 30 days, readable only by practice-hr.

nodes.label: /etc/practice-hr.env settings file
nodes.rationale: Root-only (mode 600) file holding settings and secrets, never in the unit file.

nodes.label: SITE_URL setting
nodes.rationale: Email links are built from it; unset they are relative and unusable.

nodes.label: SQLite database in WAL mode (DB_PATH)
nodes.rationale: Production puts it in /var/lib/practice-hr, outside the read-only code tree, because SQLite must write the directory holding its database.

nodes.label: TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS
nodes.rationale: Addresses whose forwarded-IP header is believed for login rate-limiting; defaults to loopback, right behind a Cloudflare tunnel; never a wildcard.

nodes.label: Excluded on purpose (spec Not done)
nodes.rationale: Buying and selling leave, statutory pay arithmetic, fit notes/return-to-work/Bradford factor, automatic deletion under retention and multi-practice are deliberately out of scope.

nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy with per-response nonce
nodes.rationale: No inline script, event-handler attributes or eval, so a future escaping bug shows as text rather than running in a colleague's session; the nonce exists only for Cloudflare's injected bot-detection script; form-action includes relying-party origins because signing in to the rota ends with a redirect after a form post; the admin is excluded because its theme needs eval; CSP_REPORT_ONLY=1 switches to report-only without a code change.

nodes.label: Least-privilege deploy layout
nodes.rationale: App runs as its own practice-hr user: code in /srv read-only, state in /var/lib/practice-hr closed to others, secrets in root-only /etc/practice-hr.env, so a request that runs code reaches only the app's own data, not its code, Cloudflare credentials or the container; every unit also runs in a systemd sandbox.

nodes.label: deploy/manage command wrapper
nodes.rationale: Runs every manage.py command as the practice-hr user with the env-file settings, exactly as the services do; plain python manage.py as root can leave root-owned WAL/-shm files the app cannot open, and sourcing the env file breaks on secret keys containing ( or $.

nodes.label: Development secret key (.dev_secret_key)
nodes.rationale: DEBUG=1 lets manage.py start with no SECRET_KEY by generating a per-checkout key into a git-ignored file; with debug off the settings refuse to run without a real key.

nodes.label: gunicorn service bound to loopback (deploy/gunicorn.service)
nodes.rationale: Binds to 127.0.0.1:8322 on purpose so only the Cloudflare tunnel reaches it; runs in a systemd sandbox scored by systemd-analyze security.

nodes.label: Off-site backup to Proxmox Backup Server (hr-pbs.service)
nodes.norm_label: off-site backup to proxmox backup server (hr-pbs.service)
nodes.rationale: The nightly copy sits on the same machine as staff and pay data, so finished copies (never the live WAL database) are pushed after each successful backup, encrypted client-side so the PBS holds no plaintext, over a private WireGuard link; the DatastoreBackup role cannot prune or delete so a compromised host cannot erase its history; the token is a file, not an environment variable, so the web service cannot read it; prune retention should match the practice retention policy.

nodes.label: Bank-holiday handling modes (closed not charged / pro-rata pot / included in annual)
nodes.norm_label: bank-holiday handling modes (closed not charged / pro-rata pot / included in annual)

nodes.label: ClosedDay (practice closure that is never charged)
nodes.norm_label: closedday (practice closure that is never charged)

nodes.label: Leave-year basis: fixed date or anniversary (29 Feb safe date)
nodes.norm_label: leave-year basis: fixed date or anniversary (29 feb safe date)

nodes.label: Pot (one employment's allowance for one type and one leave year)
nodes.norm_label: pot (one employment's allowance for one type and one leave year)
nodes.rationale: Unique per employment, absence type and year start; unit is taken from the contract when the pot opens; deliberately has no balance field.

nodes.label: Seeded absence types (AL, BH, STUDY, TOIL, SICK, MAT, PAT, SPL, ADOPT, COMP, DEP, UNPAID, OTHER)
nodes.norm_label: seeded absence types (al, bh, study, toil, sick, mat, pat, spl, adopt, comp, dep, unpaid, other)

nodes.label: AbsenceType flags drive the workflow
nodes.rationale: Types are configurable rows; paid, uses_pot, needs_approval, self_certified, calendar_label, payroll_reportable and health_sensitive decide behaviour instead of code testing a type's name.

nodes.label: Accrual integral (entitlement as a day-by-day sum over the leave year)
nodes.norm_label: accrual integral (entitlement as a day-by-day sum over the leave year)
nodes.rationale: Each active day accrues (weeks + tier extra) x contracted weekly amount / days in year, so mid-year starters and leavers, tier steps, fixed-term and concurrent contracts pro-rate naturally and a leap year accrues the same as a common year. Pure: reads people rows and policies, writes nothing.

nodes.label: Automatic bank-holiday absences
nodes.rationale: Approved auto rows are created only for bank holidays the person works under the two pot handlings and cancelled with a cancellation line when the pattern or policy stops implying them; idempotent.

nodes.label: Balance is the sum of LedgerEntry rows (no stored balance)
nodes.norm_label: balance is the sum of ledgerentry rows (no stored balance)
nodes.rationale: Nothing stores a balance; every figure is recomputed from ledger lines so history stays auditable and a correction is just another line.

nodes.label: Bank-holiday pot formula (year's bank holidays / 5 as weeks)
nodes.norm_label: bank-holiday pot formula (year's bank holidays / 5 as weeks)
nodes.rationale: Under pro-rata pot handling the number of bank holidays in the year divided by five is used as the weeks figure in the accrual integral.

nodes.label: C2 ruling: bank holidays charged only by automatic rows
nodes.norm_label: c2 ruling: bank holidays charged only by automatic rows
nodes.rationale: From the final review: ordinary range bookings skip bank holidays under every handling, overlap checks compare ordinary with ordinary and automatic with automatic, and kept automatic rows are re-costed; the spec was amended in section 4.

nodes.label: Costing a booking from the working pattern
nodes.norm_label: costing a booking from the working pattern
nodes.rationale: Cost is the sum of AM/PM units from the pattern in force each day, skipping closed days and bank holidays under closed handling; a weekend or a day with no pattern costs zero rather than erroring.

nodes.label: sync_entitlement writes the difference as one revision line
nodes.norm_label: sync_entitlement writes the difference as one revision line
nodes.rationale: Reconciles entitlement lines with accrual.entitlement by writing only the delta with a cause note; idempotent, so a second sync or a change that rounds to nothing writes nothing.

nodes.label: I1 ruling: pots open synced and the nightly bootstraps them
nodes.norm_label: i1 ruling: pots open synced and the nightly bootstraps them
nodes.rationale: pots.for_day writes the entitlement (and an AL pot's automatic bank holidays) on creation and the nightly opens current-year pots for every active employment; because for_day now writes, plan 3 must not call it on a GET.

nodes.label: Immutable ledger entries (corrections are new lines)
nodes.norm_label: immutable ledger entries (corrections are new lines)
nodes.rationale: LedgerEntry.save refuses an existing pk and delete always raises, so the ledger is append-only; every change to a pot is a visible line.

nodes.label: Leave-year boundary refusal ('Book the two leave years separately')
nodes.norm_label: leave-year boundary refusal ('book the two leave years separately')
nodes.rationale: An absence crossing the leave-year end is refused rather than drawing on two pots, keeping one absence to one pot.

nodes.label: MIDDAY partial-day cap (13:00)
nodes.rationale: A partial day is capped at the units of the halves it touches, split at 13:00, so hours booked cannot exceed what the pattern says the person works.

nodes.label: Missing policy is a ValidationError naming it, never a silent zero
nodes.norm_label: missing policy is a validationerror naming it, never a silent zero
nodes.rationale: A pot-backed type with no policy for the contract type must fail loudly with the policy named, so a misconfiguration never shows as zero entitlement.

nodes.label: Nightly safety net (nightly.run re-syncs every open pot and bank holidays)
nodes.norm_label: nightly safety net (nightly.run re-syncs every open pot and bank holidays)
nodes.rationale: Repeats the signal-driven re-sync for every open pot each night so a missed signal cannot leave an entitlement stale; hooked into hr_nightly.

nodes.label: Overlapping requested or approved absences refused in the service
nodes.norm_label: overlapping requested or approved absences refused in the service

nodes.label: Re-costing an approved absence as an adjustment line
nodes.norm_label: re-costing an approved absence as an adjustment line
nodes.rationale: After a pattern change an HR admin re-prices an approved absence; the difference is written as an ADJUSTMENT line rather than editing the booking line.

nodes.label: Sickness self-certified when shorter than seven days
nodes.norm_label: sickness self-certified when shorter than seven days
nodes.rationale: SICK needs no approval and no pot; it is recorded approved and flagged self-certified when under SELF_CERT_DAYS (7).

nodes.label: Step rounding (0.25 hour, 0.5 session, half up)
nodes.norm_label: step rounding (0.25 hour, 0.5 session, half up)
nodes.rationale: Units are two-place Decimals rounded to the policy step, half up, so entitlements and costs land on bookable amounts.

nodes.label: base.html (Site base layout)
nodes.rationale: Two theme-color meta tags (light/dark --accent) rather than a manifest's single theme_color. Loads theme.js early, the design-system CSS (fonts, tokens, components, screens) plus the generated {% palette_css %}, and passkeys.js deferred. Flash messages use role=alert for errors and role=status otherwise.

nodes.label: people/me.html (My record page)
nodes.rationale: Shows employment facts (start, continuous service, position, contracted units), the AM/PM working pattern grid and an editable personal-details form; a polite notice when no employee record is linked to the login.

nodes.label: people/retention.html (Retention report)
nodes.rationale: Lists people whose records are past their retention period, by category with days overdue. It only lists them: nothing is deleted automatically, and deletion is manual in this release.

nodes.label: people/team.html (My team page)
nodes.rationale: An approver's direct reports with position, contracted units and working-pattern total; 'Nobody reports to you today' when empty.

nodes.label: locked_out.html (Too many attempts page)
nodes.rationale: Rendered by accounts/lockout.py with status 429 when a password sign-in is refused (too many failures for this account, or against too many accounts from this address). Only the password is paused, so the page leads with the two ways in that bypass it (passkey, emailed password link) rather than with the one-hour wait.

nodes.label: login.html (Log in page)
nodes.rationale: Password form plus a 'Sign in with a passkey' button hidden until passkeys.js arms it; links to the forgotten-password flow.

nodes.label: password_reset_done.html (Check your email page)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately non-committal ('If there's a login for that address') so the page does not reveal which emails have accounts; the link works for seven days.

nodes.label: Top navigation bar (role-gated)
nodes.rationale: Desktop nav: My record, Leave, Calendar, Balances always; Approvals (with waiting_count) only when can_approve; My team only when is_approver; Admin only for HR admins or superusers; theme toggle, account link and POST logout.

nodes.label: Mobile tab bar
nodes.rationale: Phone-width equivalent of the top nav with the same role gating; less-used destinations (Balances, Calendar, Admin, theme, account, logout) sit in a 'More' details sheet.

nodes.label: Pay and NI never rendered on the employee's own or team pages
nodes.norm_label: pay and ni never rendered on the employee's own or team pages

nodes.label: Balance summary (entitlement, carried in, taken, booked, pending, expired, adjustments, remaining)
nodes.norm_label: balance summary (entitlement, carried in, taken, booked, pending, expired, adjustments, remaining)

nodes.label: Deferred to plan 3 (carry-over, expiry, TOIL earned, year end, chase, calendar, request pages, payroll, API)
nodes.norm_label: deferred to plan 3 (carry-over, expiry, toil earned, year end, chase, calendar, request pages, payroll, api)

nodes.label: LedgerEntry kinds (entitlement, revision, carry-in, expiry, booking, cancellation, TOIL earned/taken, adjustment)
nodes.norm_label: ledgerentry kinds (entitlement, revision, carry-in, expiry, booking, cancellation, toil earned/taken, adjustment)

nodes.label: Admin dashboard card (waiting requests, email not configured)
nodes.norm_label: admin dashboard card (waiting requests, email not configured)

nodes.label: Notification routing: routed manager's work email or every active HR admin
nodes.norm_label: notification routing: routed manager's work email or every active hr admin

nodes.label: Recording an absence for someone else (absence:request_for)
nodes.norm_label: recording an absence for someone else (absence:request_for)

nodes.label: TOIL earned (toil.earn writes a TOIL_EARNED line)
nodes.norm_label: toil earned (toil.earn writes a toil_earned line)

nodes.label: Absence workflow, payroll and API implementation plan
nodes.norm_label: absence workflow, payroll and api implementation plan

nodes.label: Approver's queue and decision page
nodes.rationale: The queue lists requests routed to the user's employee (all for HR admins); the decider is always recorded, an HR admin may decide anything, and an approver who is off that day can still decide.

nodes.label: Calendar shows calendar_label only; sickness category never rendered
nodes.norm_label: calendar shows calendar_label only; sickness category never rendered
nodes.rationale: Colleagues see Leave/Sick/Away; a health category appears only on the employee's own page, their manager's view and the admin.

nodes.label: The chase: requests waiting more than CHASE_AFTER_WORKING_DAYS, emailed once
nodes.norm_label: the chase: requests waiting more than chase_after_working_days, emailed once
nodes.rationale: Counts working days since the request and stamps chased_at so HR admins are emailed about each waiting request only once.

nodes.label: A decider never decides their own request
nodes.norm_label: a decider never decides their own request

nodes.label: One email door that never raises (absence.mail.send)
nodes.norm_label: one email door that never raises (absence.mail.send)
nodes.rationale: A mail relay fault must not surface in a page: send returns False, logs the failure, and the dashboard shows it.

nodes.label: Min-present warning ('Approving leaves fewer than N present')
nodes.norm_label: min-present warning ('approving leaves fewer than n present')
nodes.rationale: The decide page warns when approving would leave a team below Team.min_present on any day of the request.

nodes.label: Negative balance carries in full at year end
nodes.norm_label: negative balance carries in full at year end
nodes.rationale: A negative balance is carried as a negative carry-in and shown as such, never silently zeroed.

nodes.label: Payroll changes report (eight sheets saved with a PayrollRun)
nodes.norm_label: payroll changes report (eight sheets saved with a payrollrun)
nodes.rationale: Monthly spreadsheet for the payroll bureau: starters, leavers, contract and pay changes, sickness, unpaid, family leave and TOIL; dates and units only, never a sickness category, never pay arithmetic.

nodes.label: TOIL lots carried as TOIL_EARNED lines with their earn date, never capped
nodes.norm_label: toil lots carried as toil_earned lines with their earn date, never capped
nodes.rationale: Year end was rewritten so each unused TOIL lot keeps its earn date and expires by toil_expires_after_days rather than being capped.

nodes.label: Year end: carry to the policy cap, expire the rest
nodes.norm_label: year end: carry to the policy cap, expire the rest
nodes.rationale: close() carries the balance up to carry_over_max_weeks x contracted amount and expires the remainder; idempotent via 'year end' notes, so running twice doubles nothing.

nodes.label: Approval routing via the primary position's line manager (None = HR admin group)
nodes.norm_label: approval routing via the primary position's line manager (none = hr admin group)
nodes.rationale: route_for returns the current manager, or None when there is no manager or the manager has no current employment, which sends the request to the HR admin group.

nodes.label: Relationship-based access (self, current manager, HR admin)
nodes.norm_label: relationship-based access (self, current manager, hr admin)
nodes.rationale: Every rule about who may see and decide what lives in people.services.access.

nodes.label: Automatic bank-holiday absence row (Charge again)
nodes.rationale: Created when the pot opens and kept in step nightly; an HR admin's cancellation stands and the nightly will not re-create it.

nodes.label: Pot (one person's allowance of one type for one leave year)
nodes.norm_label: pot (one person's allowance of one type for one leave year)
nodes.rationale: Has no balance field; its balance is the sum of its ledger lines. This and next year's pots open nightly; TOIL pots open when first earned or booked.

nodes.label: TOIL (time off in lieu) claims
nodes.rationale: Earned, not accrued: rises only when a claim for time worked is approved, dated the day worked.

nodes.label: Payroll report sheets (Starters, Leavers, Contract changes, Pay changes, Sickness, Unpaid, Family leave, TOIL)
nodes.norm_label: payroll report sheets (starters, leavers, contract changes, pay changes, sickness, unpaid, family leave, toil)
nodes.rationale: Which sheet an absence reaches follows its type's flags, never its name.

nodes.label: Leaver debts
nodes.rationale: A leaver's negative balance is left untouched and reported each night until settled by adjustment.

nodes.label: What to check in January (year-end checks)
nodes.norm_label: what to check in january (year-end checks)

nodes.label: Leave ledger (append-only ledger lines)
nodes.rationale: Lines are only ever added, never edited or deleted, so every figure can be traced to lines and a mistake is put right by a new line.

nodes.label: Leaver balance rule
nodes.rationale: Counts lines dated on or before the last day plus entitlement lines whatever their date, because the pro-rating revision is written when the end date is recorded, possibly after the last day.

nodes.label: Adjust balance (adjustment line)
nodes.rationale: The ledger is immutable, so corrections are new audited adjustment lines; a closed pot refuses them, so corrections go on the current year's pot.

nodes.label: Carry-in expiry (booked by the deadline)
nodes.rationale: Booked means requested by the deadline and approved, so a slow approver never costs the employee.

nodes.label: Hand-entered carry-overs (shell)
nodes.rationale: Written as carry-in lines, not adjustments, so the policy's carry-in expiry applies; run the year end first or the nightly closes freshly filled pots.

nodes.label: TOIL lots and expiry (first in, first out)
nodes.norm_label: toil lots and expiry (first in, first out)
nodes.rationale: Each earned line is a lot carried forward uncapped keeping its earned date, so its deadline runs on unchanged.

nodes.label: Year-end close
nodes.rationale: Idempotent: each step looks for its own earlier line; one expiry line takes the whole remaining balance so a closed pot stands at zero, and a closed pot takes no more lines.

nodes.label: Deciding a request (approval routing)
nodes.rationale: Nobody decides their own request; requests with no line manager go to the HR admins; approving re-costs and writes the booking line in one transaction.

nodes.label: Health sensitive flag
nodes.rationale: Kind of sickness and dates restricted to HR admins and the line manager; opening one in the admin is audited; the API always says Sick and payroll reports dates only.

nodes.label: Audit log
nodes.rationale: Read-only; Change entries for service-function field changes and Viewed entries for restricted sections; keeps the actor's email as text so later email changes do not rewrite it.

nodes.label: Continuous service date
nodes.rationale: Service length is reckoned from it, never the start date; leaving it blank on a returner understates service and gets tiers wrong.

nodes.label: Contract
nodes.rationale: The contracted amount on a day is the sum of every contract active that day (contracts.contracted_amount()).

nodes.label: Employment (spell of work)
nodes.rationale: Everything dated hangs off it; a returner gets a new Employment row. Spells cannot overlap; saving an end date cancels absences starting after it.

nodes.label: Line manager (approval routing)
nodes.rationale: Self-management and reporting-line loops are refused because a loop would leave nobody able to approve either person's requests; blank sends requests to the HR admins.

nodes.label: Pay record (restricted)
nodes.rationale: Can be amended in full, unlike positions and contracts, because it records what was decided rather than a live contractual state.

nodes.label: Working pattern
nodes.rationale: Versioned by effective_from; the pattern in force is the latest version on or before the day (patterns.pattern_on()).

nodes.label: Admin status (is_hr_admin)
nodes.rationale: is_staff follows it automatically; HR admins cannot see or grant superuser.

nodes.label: Delegated approval while a manager is away
nodes.norm_label: delegated approval while a manager is away

nodes.label: One-unit-at-a-time rule
nodes.rationale: Concurrent contracts must share a unit so contracted_amount() stays a single meaningful number; mixing sessions and hours would add two different things.

nodes.label: Positions and contracts only end
nodes.rationale: A change is a new row plus an end date on the old one, so the record shows what was true on any past day; a refused row stops the whole save.

nodes.label: Primary position rule
nodes.rationale: Exactly one primary position per day; its line manager routes approvals, so a secondary role ticked primary would make the wrong person the approver.

nodes.label: Pattern total-differs warning
nodes.rationale: A pattern not matching the contract is a legitimate temporary state (phased return), so it warns rather than refuses, keeping a mismatch from being silent.

nodes.label: Nothing is deleted principle
nodes.rationale: No delete button anywhere in People or Login accounts so history stays intact whatever changes.

nodes.label: Restricted data is gated and logged
nodes.norm_label: restricted data is gated and logged
nodes.rationale: NI numbers and pay records are visible to HR admins only and viewing them writes an audit entry.

nodes.label: Self-management and reporting cycles refused at the service
nodes.norm_label: self-management and reporting cycles refused at the service

nodes.label: Concurrent contracts must share a unit; contracted amount is their sum
nodes.norm_label: concurrent contracts must share a unit; contracted amount is their sum
nodes.rationale: Contracts may overlap and the amount on a day sums them, but mixing sessions and hours is refused; touching ranges (31 March / 1 April) do not clash.

nodes.label: FTE sums each contract's own weekly_amount / full_time_weekly
nodes.norm_label: fte sums each contract's own weekly_amount / full_time_weekly
nodes.rationale: Replaced dividing the total by the first contract's full-time figure, which was incoherent when two same-unit types coexist.

nodes.label: Pattern total differing from the contract warns, never refuses
nodes.norm_label: pattern total differing from the contract warns, never refuses
nodes.rationale: Part-timers' patterns and contracts drift by design, so a mismatch saves with a warning.

nodes.label: Deployment: gunicorn on loopback 8322, nightly timer 01:30, backup with media
nodes.norm_label: deployment: gunicorn on loopback 8322, nightly timer 01:30, backup with media

nodes.norm_label: hr_nightly runs every app's nightly job

nodes.label: OpenID Connect provider for the practice's apps
nodes.norm_label: openid connect provider for the practice's apps
nodes.rationale: django-oauth-toolkit serves OIDC with RS256 and consent skipped; only email and employee_id leave the system through sign-in; with no RSA key in the environment /o/ answers 404.

nodes.label: The rota signs in with the practice account
nodes.norm_label: the rota signs in with the practice account
nodes.rationale: The rota's mozilla-django-oidc backend matches the email claim case-insensitively to an existing user or creates one with no usable password; is_rota_admin stays local to the rota.

nodes.label: register_oidc_client prints the client secret once
nodes.norm_label: register_oidc_client prints the client secret once
nodes.rationale: The secret is stored hashed and cannot be shown again, so it is printed once for pasting into the relying party's environment file.

nodes.label: Secrets from the environment only
nodes.rationale: No key, token or password in the repository or any log line; settings read them from /etc/practice-hr.env.

nodes.label: Separate Django project mirroring the rota's conventions
nodes.norm_label: separate django project mirroring the rota's conventions
nodes.rationale: Practice HR reuses the rota's stack and conventions (SQLite WAL, unfold admin, no build step, secrets from the environment) so one person can run both.

nodes.label: files.sniff (content sniffing)
nodes.rationale: The extension says what the file claims to be; the bytes must agree, so an HTML page saved as .pdf is refused and nothing written.

nodes.label: policies.owed
nodes.rationale: Only the current version of each applicable policy is owed, so a policy reissued before a starter signed the old one never leaves the older version owed.

nodes.label: Migration people 0013_positiontitle (hand-written data migration)
nodes.rationale: Written by hand, not makemigrations alone, so existing free-text titles become one PositionTitle row each and the migration is reversible end to end.

nodes.label: Review Focus: five conditions no happy-path test exercises
nodes.norm_label: review focus: five conditions no happy-path test exercises

nodes.label: Check (append-only; a renewal is a new row)
nodes.norm_label: check (append-only; a renewal is a new row)

nodes.label: CheckType (admin-defined, required by position title)
nodes.rationale: The list (right to work, DBS, references, occupational health, Hep B, indemnity, professional registration) is right today and will change.

nodes.label: documents.File (opaque path, SHA-256, superseded never deleted)
nodes.norm_label: documents.file (opaque path, sha-256, superseded never deleted)

nodes.label: documents.Policy and PolicyVersion
nodes.rationale: Compliance, not convenience: a new version must be signed again by everyone it applies to.

nodes.label: PositionTitle
nodes.rationale: Position.title was free text; check types, policies and checklist templates all target a title, so titles become rows.

nodes.label: Signature (immutable, one per employee and version)
nodes.norm_label: signature (immutable, one per employee and version)

nodes.label: DBS: no certificate image stored
nodes.rationale: Following the DBS code of practice, only the certificate number, issue date, disclosure level and update-service flag are kept.

nodes.norm_label: api hardening (hmac token compare, csrf_exempt, no-store, hr.w001)

nodes.norm_label: accounts app copied from the rota at commit f1cdc4d

nodes.norm_label: api absences window uses overlap, not containment

nodes.label: Read API for the rota (people, patterns, absences)
nodes.norm_label: read api for the rota (people, patterns, absences)
nodes.rationale: Three read-only JSON views behind a bearer token; no push; the rota consumes them.

nodes.label: PolicyForm._check_year (leave-year lock on add)
nodes.rationale: A backdated policy add with a different leave year double-counts days exactly as the locked edit would.

nodes.label: My absences always lists still-requested absences

nodes.norm_label: leaver's late toil claim lands on the pot of their last day (_pot_day)

nodes.label: Absence Policy and PolicyTier (rules as data)
nodes.norm_label: absence policy and policytier (rules as data)

nodes.label: accrual.entitlement (day-by-day integral)
nodes.rationale: Service tiers stepping mid-year, fixed terms ending, starters, leavers and hours changes are all one calculation.

nodes.label: LedgerEntry (balance is the sum of lines)
nodes.norm_label: ledgerentry (balance is the sum of lines)
nodes.rationale: Tiered allowances, payroll reporting and audit all need to answer why a number is what it is; lines are never edited and corrections are new lines.

nodes.label: Payroll changes report and PayrollRun
nodes.rationale: Payroll is an external bureau taking a monthly changes report; the system records dates and units and does no statutory pay arithmetic, keeping SSP, SMP and OSP rules out of the codebase.

nodes.label: Blank means never; a 0-day expiry is refused
nodes.norm_label: blank means never; a 0-day expiry is refused
nodes.rationale: toil.check, year_end._toil_lots and year_end.expire_carry_in read 0 three different ways; refusing 0 makes them agree.

nodes.label: Minimal health data (dates and a coarse category)
nodes.norm_label: minimal health data (dates and a coarse category)
nodes.rationale: No free text, no fit notes; those are a later, restricted feature.

nodes.label: Entitlement in weeks per year
nodes.rationale: One formula covers both units (sessions and hours) and pro-rates part-timers without a special case.

nodes.label: admin/index.html (Admin dashboard override)
nodes.rationale: Extends unfold's own admin index (Django skips this file when it resolves the name again), adding the absence workflow's card above the app list, then {{ block.super }}.

nodes.label: Presence headcount (N of M present)
nodes.rationale: Per working day the team calendar shows how many of the headcount are present, omitted on weekends and bank holidays, so approvers can judge cover; the decide page reuses the same per-day off/present data for the request's dates.

nodes.label: Emails that did not go list
nodes.norm_label: emails that did not go list
nodes.rationale: Surfaces the most recent failed outgoing emails (time, subject, error), newest first, so a silent relay failure is visible to admins.

nodes.label: Outgoing email not configured notice
nodes.rationale: Warns admins that requests and decisions are not being emailed, so people will need to check the site.

nodes.label: Leave requests and TOIL claims waiting card
nodes.norm_label: leave requests and toil claims waiting card
nodes.rationale: Lists leave requests and TOIL claims that have waited more than chase_after working days, each linking to its decide page, so HR can chase stalled approvals.

nodes.label: Dual month view (grid vs day list)
nodes.norm_label: dual month view (grid vs day list)
nodes.rationale: The same month is rendered twice: a 7-column grid above 640px and, below it, a list of only the days with someone off (and bank holidays); screens.css shows one. Uses visually-hidden captions, day names and chip titles plus aria-current=date for accessibility on both views.

nodes.label: div.html (Site form layout)
nodes.rationale: The site's form layout (config/forms.py): what is wrong with the form as a whole first, then the hidden fields, then each field through field.html.

nodes.label: field.html (Design-system field markup)
nodes.rationale: One field in the design system's markup (components.css), shared by form.as_div and field.as_field_group: label (no colon), control, help, then each error as an alert. A checkbox sits inside its label; radios and checkbox lists are a fieldset with options in a row. Dates, times, numbers and short text are .field-short so they do not stretch.

nodes.label: password_reset_confirm.html (Set password from link page)
nodes.rationale: One template serves both the invitation ('Welcome, choose a password') and the reset, switched on is_invitation; setting the password signs the person straight in. An invalid or used link offers to request another or ask an HR admin.

nodes.label: password_reset_email.txt (Password reset email body)
nodes.rationale: Single-use reset link with expiry; 'If that wasn't you, ignore this, your password stays as it is.'

nodes.label: Approver link built from SITE_URL + notify.DECIDE_PATH (hr.W002)
nodes.norm_label: approver link built from site_url + notify.decide_path (hr.w002)

nodes.label: Practice HR system
nodes.rationale: HR software for a GP practice (people, contracts, working patterns, absence and leave, sign-in for the practice's apps) built to replace BreatheHR; the rota reads people, patterns and absences from it.

nodes.label: Design specs (docs/superpowers/specs/)
nodes.rationale: One spec per piece of work in build order; the first is the foundation and absence system.

nodes.label: Shared reminder engine
nodes.rationale: One place for 'something expires or has lapsed', shared by registration checks, onboarding checks and training compliance.

nodes.label: documents sign view (password or passkey re-authentication)
nodes.norm_label: documents sign view (password or passkey re-authentication)

nodes.label: AppRole (per-application admin flag on the HR login)
nodes.norm_label: approle (per-application admin flag on the hr login)
nodes.rationale: The per-app role carries admin only; access to an app is any active HR login. An access flag can be added later if wanted.

nodes.label: Break-glass: remove PRACTICE_HR_URL and restart the rota
nodes.norm_label: break-glass: remove practice_hr_url and restart the rota

nodes.norm_label: sign-in through hr only (practice_hr_url set): rota passwords and passkeys closed

nodes.label: import_logins management command (HR)
nodes.rationale: Sets a password only where the HR login has none, so a password chosen on HR is never overwritten; the hash is copied as is, never re-hashed.

nodes.label: Login export JSON file (mode 0600, deleted after import)
nodes.norm_label: login export json file (mode 0600, deleted after import)

nodes.label: PracticeAccountBackend (rota OIDC backend)
nodes.rationale: Checks the admin claim with `is True` rather than truthiness so a stray string could never grant admin; superusers sign in through HR like everyone else.

nodes.label: accounts app (moved from the rota: login, invitations, passkeys, axes lockout)
nodes.norm_label: accounts app (moved from the rota: login, invitations, passkeys, axes lockout)

nodes.label: OpenID Connect provider (django-oauth-toolkit, code flow, sub/email/employee_id claims)
nodes.norm_label: openid connect provider (django-oauth-toolkit, code flow, sub/email/employee_id claims)

nodes.label: Rota (GP rota app, OIDC relying party)
nodes.norm_label: rota (gp rota app, oidc relying party)

nodes.label: Rota change: Sign in with the practice account
nodes.norm_label: rota change: sign in with the practice account
nodes.rationale: The only rota change in this release; the rota password form stays only for the superuser and rota passkeys are retired once every account has signed in through HR.

nodes.label: Shared Django default password hashers
nodes.rationale: Neither repository sets PASSWORD_HASHERS, so a hash string moves between them unchanged.

nodes.label: HR system as the identity provider
nodes.norm_label: hr system as the identity provider
nodes.rationale: GPs will not accept two logins; HR holds every employee anyway and the passkey, invitation and lockout work already exists in accounts, so no shared package is needed.

nodes.label: Separate Django project in its own repository
nodes.norm_label: separate django project in its own repository
nodes.rationale: The rota models GPs only and holds almost no personal data; an HR system covers every employee and holds health, DBS and bank data. Putting it in the rota would invert the population and undo the decision that the rota holds no leave balances.

nodes.label: SQLite WAL and a filesystem document store
nodes.norm_label: sqlite wal and a filesystem document store
nodes.rationale: At one practice's headcount it is plenty and the backup tooling exists; Postgres only if concurrency ever shows.

nodes.label: Signing with re-authentication (password or passkey)
nodes.rationale: A signature should prove presence, not just a session; a wrong password counts towards the lockout.

nodes.label: Monthly payroll changes run
nodes.rationale: For a month, generates a spreadsheet for the payroll bureau covering starters, leavers, contract and pay changes, sickness dates, unpaid leave, family leave and TOIL. Generating a month again replaces its file with the latest figures and is recorded as another run, with per-sheet row counts and who generated it (or the command line).

nodes.label: No service writes to a closed pot; ledger.adjust on the current pot is the remedy
nodes.norm_label: no service writes to a closed pot; ledger.adjust on the current pot is the remedy

nodes.label: Keeping-in-touch (KIT) days
nodes.rationale: KIT days are recorded against an existing absence from My absences, with the date constrained to that absence's start and end dates, and listed under it.

nodes.label: Automatic bank-holiday absence row
nodes.rationale: Bank holidays are charged automatically as approved absence rows made by the nightly job. Once such a row is cancelled it stays cancelled and the nightly does not recreate it (so an admin's cancellation is not silently undone). To charge the day later, Charge again makes a new automatic row and approves it, only if the person's working pattern and policy still charge that day; the old row stays cancelled for history.

nodes.label: Cancellation line returns cost to pot
nodes.norm_label: cancellation line returns cost to pot
nodes.rationale: Cancelling an approved absence does not delete its charge: the cost goes back to its pot with a separate cancellation ledger line, recorded as the acting user.

nodes.label: API fixed-window rate limit (API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, 429)
nodes.rationale: Exists only to slow a guessing client, so it is counted before the token check and a per-gunicorn-worker LocMemCache is acceptable; default raised to 600 because a rota poll costs 2 plus one /patterns request per person.

nodes.label: Leaver audit note lists not-cancelled absences first (_cancel_after)
nodes.norm_label: leaver audit note lists not-cancelled absences first (_cancel_after)
nodes.rationale: AuditEntry.note is 200 characters and the not-cancelled part came last, so the part HR most needs was lost; truncation now ends with an ellipsis so it is visible.

nodes.label: Contract (may overlap; contracted_amount is their sum)
nodes.norm_label: contract (may overlap; contracted_amount is their sum)
nodes.rationale: '18.75 hours permanent plus 18.75 hours fixed term for twelve months' is a real contract.

nodes.label: Employment (dated spell, continuous service date)
nodes.rationale: People leave and come back; reckonable service is not always the start date.

nodes.label: Read API for the rota (/api/v1/)
nodes.rationale: Shape fixed in spec 1 though the rota consumes it in spec 2; read-only so a rota fault cannot change HR data.

nodes.label: WorkingPattern and PatternDay
nodes.rationale: Working patterns live in HR and are the master so the admin never records a pattern in two places.

nodes.label: Onboarding, offboarding and documents implementation plan
nodes.norm_label: onboarding, offboarding and documents implementation plan

nodes.label: Effective dating (from-date, optional to-date, 'as of a day')
nodes.norm_label: effective dating (from-date, optional to-date, 'as of a day')
nodes.rationale: Employments, positions, contracts, patterns, pay records and policies carry dates so any question can be asked as of a day.

nodes.label: Services are the only writers
nodes.rationale: All writes to people and absence go through */services/, never a view, form save() or the admin; the admin is a thin layer over the services, so every write is audited and transactional.

nodes.label: checks.state and the check status rules
nodes.norm_label: checks.state and the check status rules

nodes.norm_label: compliance django app (reminderschedule, remindersent, schedule, digest)

nodes.norm_label: mail.py email delivery (never raises into a page)

nodes.label: ReminderSchedule (start 60, every 30, overdue every 7 days)
nodes.rationale: A practice setting so HR tunes the cadence without a code change; per-check-type cadences are not done until shown necessary.

nodes.label: Retention categories: checks, files, signatures
nodes.rationale: Nothing is deleted automatically; the retention report lists what is due and a person deletes it.

nodes.label: compliance package (due-items contract and digest)
nodes.rationale: Three focused apps sharing one 'what is due' contract and one morning digest, not a generic requirement engine: each reads like the thing it is, and the digest is what spec 4 plugs into.

nodes.label: Two-step request without JavaScript (validate, show cost and balance, confirm)
nodes.norm_label: two-step request without javascript (validate, show cost and balance, confirm)

nodes.label: Balances for this leave year and next, linked to ledger lines
nodes.norm_label: balances for this leave year and next, linked to ledger lines

nodes.label: Pages never write on GET (pots.lookup, balances.rows)
nodes.norm_label: pages never write on get (pots.lookup, balances.rows)
nodes.rationale: Because pots.for_day opens and syncs a pot, pages read through lookup/rows and the nightly opens this and next year's pots ahead of time.

nodes.label: Append-only leave ledger
nodes.rationale: Ledger lines are never edited or deleted. A balance adjustment is written as the acting admin, dated today, as one adjustment line through ledger.adjust; to undo it, adjust again. A closed pot (its leave year has ended) should not be adjusted: adjust the current year's pot instead. Keeps a full audit trail of every balance change.

nodes.label: Balance figures drill down to ledger lines
nodes.norm_label: balance figures drill down to ledger lines
nodes.rationale: Each balance figure (entitlement, carried in, taken, booked, waiting, expired, adjustments) links to the filtered ledger lines behind it, and the ledger offers Show all. A non-accruing type such as TOIL with no pot yet shows zero figures without links.

nodes.label: Waiting requests are not ledger lines
nodes.norm_label: waiting requests are not ledger lines
nodes.rationale: Requests waiting for a decision are not written to the ledger until they are approved, so the Waiting figure's drill-down lists the pending absences instead of ledger entries.

nodes.label: invitation_email.txt (Invitation email body)
nodes.rationale: Single-use set-password link with an expiry date; if expired, ask the sending admin (contact) or use 'Forgotten your password?' on the login page; 'nothing happens until the link is used' if unexpected.

nodes.label: Retention report (RETENTION_DAYS per category)
nodes.rationale: Lists leavers whose personal, pay, health or audit data is past its retention period; deletion stays manual in this release.

nodes.label: Effective dating (from-date and optional to-date)
nodes.rationale: Employments, positions, contracts, patterns and pay records are dated rows, so any calculation can ask what was true on a day.

nodes.norm_label: nothing in people is ever deleted; rows end
